{{Short description|Theorem in topology}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Esenin-Volpin's theorem''' states that [[Base (topology)#Weight and character|weight]] of an infinite [[compact space|compact]] [[dyadic space]] is the supremum of the weights of its points. It was introduced by {{harvs|txt|authorlink=Alexander Esenin-Volpin|first= Alexander|last= Esenin-Volpin|year=1949}}.<ref>{{citation |last=Esenin-Volpin |first=A. S. |title=On the relation between the local and integral weight in dyadic bicompacta |journal=Doklady Akademii Nauk SSSR |volume=68 |pages=441–444 |year=1949 |series=New Series |language=Russian |mr=0031029 |zbl=0033.02203}}</ref> It was generalized by Efimov in 1965<ref>{{citation |last=Efimov |first=B. A. |title=Dyadic bicompacta |journal=Trudy Moskov. Mat. Obšč. |volume=14 |pages=211–247 |year=1965 |language=Russian |mr=0202105}}</ref> and Turzański in 1992.<ref>{{citation |last=Turzański |first=Marian |title=Strong sequences, binary families and Esenin-Volpin's theorem |journal=Comment.Math.Univ.Carolinae |volume=33 |issue=3 |pages=563–569 |year=1992 |url=https://eudml.org/doc/247365 |mr=1209298 |zbl=0796.54031}}</ref>
